facts.fact: A ministry of communications document seen by Bloomberg says Egypt intends to allocate up to USD 860 million a year from the general budget, from FY2026/27 to the end of 2030, for data centres, computing infrastructure, data security and AI use in state companies; the document gives no event date, so the story's published date is used.
facts.system: Data centres and computing infrastructure programme, general budget, FY2026/27-2030

note: Allocation is stated as an intention ('intends to allocate'); no prior-year figure, so no rose or fell.

facts.fact: The Minister of Planning told the House of Representatives that EGP 13 billion of public investment is allocated to the ICT sector in the 2025/2026 plan, of which EGP 9 billion is financed from the state's general budget; the document gives no date for the presentation, so its published date is used.
facts.system: Communications and Information Technology sector public investment, FY2025/26

facts.fact: The Minister of Planning told the House of Representatives that EGP 13 billion of public investment is allocated to the ICT sector in the 2025/2026 plan, of which EGP 9 billion is financed from the state's general budget; the document gives no date for the presentation, so its published date is used.
facts.system: Communications and Information Technology sector public investment, FY2025/26

facts.fact: Public ICT investment fell to EGP 13 bn in FY 2025/26 from EGP 85 bn a year earlier, according to a government document seen by EnterpriseAM.

note: Figure is public ICT sector investment, not stated as the digital ministry's budget lines.

facts.fact: The House Plan and Budget Committee approved the 2026/27 appropriations for the general office of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, estimated at about 23.3 billion pounds against 19.69 billion as the actual estimate for the current year.
facts.system: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology budget 2026/27

facts.fact: The parliamentary planning and budget committee approved NTRA's 2026/27 budget, which targets transferring about EGP 5.7 billion to the Universal Service Fund to finance projects of the national telecom and information plan and rural infrastructure, as reported on 4 June 2026.
